I am Dr. Agent. Given your history of AIDS and symptoms of decreased vision with black spots in your right eye, I need to ask: Do you see a shower of floaters, flashes of light, or a specific curtain-like shadow over your vision?

REQUEST TEST: Dilated Fundoscopic Exam
REQUEST IMAGES: Right Eye Fundus

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Granular yellow-white opacities around the retinal vessels and multiple areas of dot-blot hemorrhages

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) Retinitis

The granular yellow-white opacities and hemorrhages you described are classic signs of CMV retinitis, a common ocular opportunistic infection in patients with advanced AIDS. The presence of dot-blot hemorrhages alongside the opacities confirms the diagnosis without needing further testing.
